OIML-CS: Scheme A = issuing authority issues certificate based on test report; Scheme B = MAA. Actually the OIML Certification System has two schemes: Scheme A (OIML certificate system, basic) and Scheme B (MAA - Mutual Acceptance Arrangement). This cert mentions "OIML — MUTUAL ACCEPTANCE ARRANGEMENT" logo... but the cert itself is a standard OIML Certificate of Conformity. Hmm. The MAA logo appears. NMi Certin is an MAA participating authority for R76? Actually the MAA logo at bottom suggests this. But the certificate format "R76/2006-NL1-13.11" with "OIML Issuing Authority NL1" is the classic pre-MAA format. I'll say scheme "A" since it's a standard OIML Certificate of Conformity from an Issuing Authority. Hmm, but MAA logo... The MAA certificates typically say "OIML MAA Certificate". This says "OIML Certificate of Conformity" — that's Scheme A. I'll go with "A".
